profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the Quant Strategy Research team and the Portfolio Solutions team at an asset manager that is preparing a client-facing research note and dashboard update on dynamic connectedness in global supply chain infrastructure portfolios. The note summarizes a TVP-VAR analysis from January 5, 2010 to June 29, 2023, focusing on ESG-linked infrastructure portfolios, spillovers from WTI, BDI, and VIX, and changes before versus after COVID-19. The agenda is to align on which research outputs will feed the client note and dashboard, which file versions and classifications will be used, how the hedge exhibits will be packaged, and when the final handoff occurs before a Monday publication. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the shared deliverables, ownership of the exhibits, and the timing of the final upload, even though several second-order assumptions remain misaligned.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Time-series econometrics, portfolio risk modeling, spillover analysis, and ESG-linked infrastructure research
members.background: Elena leads thematic quant publications for the firm's multi-asset research group and previously built macro risk models on a sell-side strategy desk.
members.private_state: She wants the client materials to stay faithful to the working paper's methodology and is trying to avoid last-minute requests that would force her team to rerun classifications or restate charts.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to ESG groups in this project, they mean the fixed portfolio classifications used throughout the 2010-2023 model to avoid look-ahead bias.
A 'connectedness table' is the research table of average net directional connectedness over a named subperiod, not a latest-point dashboard snapshot.
The 'hedge results' for this study are the hedge ratio and hedge effectiveness outputs for portfolio exposure to WTI, BDI, and VIX, not broader cross-portfolio examples.
The June 29 data cut means the vendor-corrected weekly panel pulled the next morning after routine end-of-day restatements, even if a draft daily snapshot already exists elsewhere.

members.name: Daniel Ruiz
members.expertise: Client reporting, investment content packaging, dashboard operations, and cross-team launch coordination
members.background: Daniel manages how research outputs are translated into client-facing notes and portal updates and previously worked in investment communications and product operations.
members.private_state: He needs a clean, consistent Monday release with minimal redesign work and is trying to preserve the existing dashboard structure and labels that sales already knows.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to ESG groups in client materials, they mean the current vendor-labeled ESG buckets already used on the dashboard and factsheets.
A 'connectedness table' is the current-state view used by clients, typically the latest rolling-window reading rather than a subperiod average.
The 'hedge results' section should include any hedge examples useful for clients, including portfolio-to-portfolio pairings if they fit the story.
The June 29 data cut is the market-close snapshot already loaded into the portal draft, since that is the operationally standard version for publication prep.

misalignment_points.topic: Which portfolios count as the 'high-ESG' group
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss the 'high-ESG portfolios' or 'top ESG bucket' as if it is a single stable set of funds.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the frozen ESG portfolio grouping used consistently across the historical model window so that the analysis does not change composition over time.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means the latest client-facing ESG bucket labels from the current vendor mapping used on the dashboard as of June 2023.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both regard ESG grouping as already standardized, and because the labels sound identical, neither sees a reason to clarify whether they mean the historical research classification or the current reporting classification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the client note and dashboard need the 'connectedness table.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means a table of average net total directional connectedness over the pre-COVID and post-COVID subperiods, matching the research note structure.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means the latest rolling-window connectedness snapshot that populates the dashboard's current-state card.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In both research and reporting workflows, the phrase 'connectedness table' is routine shorthand, and each person's version is plausible enough that the surface agreement feels complete.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the 'hedge results'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the 'hedge results' should be included in the materials.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena includes only the study's factor hedge outputs: hedge ratios and hedge effectiveness for infrastructure portfolios hedged with WTI, BDI, and VIX exposures.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes the hedge section can also include portfolio-to-portfolio hedging examples or peer-pair exhibits if they help sales tell the story, because those sit naturally beside factor hedges in prior client packs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see portfolio hedging and factor hedging as part of the same broader hedging narrative, so the boundary of the section remains implicit rather than explicitly negotiated.

misalignment_points.topic: Which file version counts as the 'June 29 cut'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to use the 'June 29 cut' or the 'final June 29 pack' for publication.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena plans to use the vendor-corrected panel downloaded on June 30 morning that still has June 29 as the end date but may differ slightly from the initial close snapshot.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes the existing June 29 close snapshot already sitting in the portal draft is the publication version unless someone explicitly says there is a replacement.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The end date is identical in both workflows, and each team has a normal operational convention for what counts as the dated file, so the version distinction stays invisible during a competent coordination call.
